title.t: Two entries for one event disagree

when.t: A new entry for a client has a value different from the most recent entry of the same kind of event.

steps.t: Agent 14 keeps both; nothing is overwritten.
It marks the new entry with the disagreement, naming the field and the earlier entry.
Nobody is alerted; the mark is on the entry for whoever reads it.

you_see.t: Both entries in the history, the second marked as disagreeing.

test.t: A client asks to be texted, then to be emailed instead. Both channel-change entries stand; the second is marked on the channel.

title.t: A new inquiry may be someone already on record

when.t: A new inquiry has the same phone or email (in any format) as a lead already on record under another thread; the name plays no part.

steps.t: Nothing is merged. Agent 01 holds the new inquiry and asks the authorized user: continue treats it as a separate person and scores it; cancel closes it.
Phone numbers are compared as digits, so different formatting still matches.

never.t: Merge records whose identity is not confirmed.

you_see.t: A held inquiry naming the record it may duplicate.

test.t: Avery Synth inquires; then "A. Synthe" inquires with the same phone.

title.t: A report covers a gap in the record

when.t: The end-of-day books run and a client has consent, interests, an agreement or a verification on file but no log entry.

steps.t: The rule: the books list that client under logging gaps; nothing is filled in.
steps.src: tuple:14-03; dispatcher/listing_spokes.py::logging_gaps = sorted(ctx for ctx in contexts_with_side_state

steps.t: No way in since 2026-10-28: every change to consent, interests, an agreement or a verification now has a log entry behind it (on a frozen record an opt-out is recorded and every other change waits), so no message leaves a client in that state. The check itself is tested with the state set directly.

title.t: A client's consent differs by channel

when.t: A client has said no on one channel and later asks to be reached on it.

steps.t: The no stands: a later yes never lifts a no on its own. Other channels keep their own answers.
Agent 11 does not confirm the change to the client; it asks the authorized user to record a reconfirmation if the client really wants it.
Only the authorized user's signed consent record marked as reconfirmed by the client lifts a no.

never.t: Relax a channel's no without a reconfirmation.

you_see.t: A question saying the opt-out stands and how to record a reconfirmation.

test.t: A lead gives consent yes for call and email, no for text, then writes "Please text me from now on".

title.t: Someone asks to delete a record

when.t: The authorized user's signed setting asks to delete a client's record.

steps.t: Agent 14 deletes nothing. It freezes the record and raises a legal-line alert.

While frozen, an opt-out still takes effect and is recorded; any other change waits until the freeze is lifted, nothing changes meanwhile, and the authorized user is told; a write that changes nothing is refused and the authorized user is told of each attempt. Only a signed release lifts the freeze, and the waiting changes are then applied in the order they came (owner decision of 2026-10-28).

never.t: Delete a record on its own.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert about the deletion request.

test.t: A lead is captured; then the authorized user asks to delete the record.

title.t: Two records look like the same person

when.t: A new inquiry has the same phone or email (in any format) as a lead already on record under another thread; the name plays no part.

steps.t: Agent 01 holds the new inquiry and asks the authorized user, naming the earlier record.
There is no way to merge two records: continue treats it as a separate person, cancel closes the new thread.

never.t: Merge two client records on its own.

you_see.t: A held inquiry: continue means a separate person.

test.t: Avery Synth inquires with (216) 555-0101, then again with +1 216 555 0101.

when.t: A fact about a client changes.

steps.t: Agent 14 adds a new entry; it has no way to edit or overwrite an entry.

never.t: Edit or remove an earlier entry.

you_see.t: Both entries in the history, in order.

test.t: The authorized user records email consent yes, then email consent no: two entries.

title.t: Imported data conflicts with the record

when.t: Data imported from another system disagrees with the record.

steps.t: The rule: the record wins and the differences are flagged.
No way in: there is no import. The check that would flag it is the one in 14-01.

never.t: Let an import overwrite the record.

title.t: An agent asks for a client record it is not routed to

when.t: An agent other than 01, 11, 13 or 15 asks Agent 14 for a client record.

steps.t: The dispatcher refuses it before Agent 14 sees it: that request is not on the agent's track.

never.t: Hand a record to an agent with no route for it.

you_see.t: A refusal on the audit log.

test.t: Standing in as Agent 06, the test asks Agent 14 for a lead's record.

title.t: A record is frozen for a deletion question

when.t: Something tries to write to a frozen record.

steps.t: Agent 14 records no entry for the change: it is not an opt-out, so it waits until the freeze is lifted, and the authorized user is told it waits.
steps.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes.py::def _frozen_write(self, ctx: str, env: Envelope):; dispatcher/listing_spokes.py:512-518; check:14-10:envelope.persisted:clarification.request

steps.t: An opt-out arriving while frozen still takes effect and is recorded; any other change, and the flags it carries, wait (owner decision of 2026-10-28; before, the entry was refused but the flags in it changed anyway).
Agent 11 sees from Agent 14 that the record is frozen and confirms nothing to the client (before 2026-10-28 it confirmed the change).

never.t: Delete or quietly keep writing to a frozen record.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert about the deletion request; a note that the client's change waits while the record is frozen; nothing confirmed to the client.

test.t: A lead is captured with consent on every channel; the record is frozen by a deletion request; the client then asks to be texted.

when.t: The authorized user signs an access grant.

steps.t: Agent 14 keeps exactly who, until when, and a custody reference.
A grant with any other field, or a value that looks like the code itself ("code", "combo", "pin" and similar words), is rejected whole.

you_see.t: The grant kept; a note for each rejected grant.

test.t: Three grants for Pat Inspector until October 20: one with custody reference "lockbox code 4411" (rejected), one with a code field (rejected), one with custody reference KEY-7 (kept).

title.t: An access window ends without being closed

when.t: On a daily run, an access grant's end date has passed and the authorized user has not closed it.

steps.t: Agent 14 asks the authorized user, once, to confirm the key is back or the code changed and then sign it closed.

you_see.t: One question naming the party and the custody reference.

test.t: A grant ends October 16; the daily run runs October 17 and 18.

title.t: A client record cannot be filed in the client's drawer

when.t: Filing a copy of a record entry in the client's drawer fails.

steps.t: The failure is recorded on the audit log and held for the authorized user; the record entry itself stands. (A system run with no drawer store files nothing and records nothing about it.)

you_see.t: A question saying the drawer filing was refused.

test.t: A lead arrives under the thread name "Jane Synth"; a name with a space cannot be a drawer folder.

title.t: The authorized user records a client's consent

when.t: The authorized user signs a consent record for a client.

steps.t: Each channel is set as signed (call, text, email; yes or no).
A channel the client opted out of stays no unless the record says the client reconfirmed; the authorized user is told which.
A malformed record is rejected whole.

never.t: Lift an opt-out without the client's reconfirmation on record.

you_see.t: Notes for a rejected record and for a kept no.

test.t: A lead says no to text. The authorized user signs text and email yes (text stays no, and the authorized user is told), then text "maybe" (rejected), then text yes marked reconfirmed (applied).
